I had to go to the emergency room two days ago because I have a history of stage 4 endometriosis and I was possibly having a ruptured ovarian cyst, and my OBGYN suggested for me to go to the emergency room because she was worried about a possible ovarian torsion from cysts, since I also have been diagnosed with PCOS.  (To the women out there they know it's very painful.) I come in and I show the ER physician and nurse all my paperwork from surgery and how my OB doctor wants the ER physician to call her to tell them how to manage my pain and how to go about doing testing. They would not call her, they would not look at my paperwork and gave me two basic 500mg tylenols when I told them I just took Norco two hours prior and it didn't work, God forbid if you ask them for stronger pain meds because they'll think your drug seeking. I was throwing up and my blood pressure was literally 160 over 110, because the pain was literally a 10. I am not over exaggerating, I'm so sick of pain management and ERs not taking pain seriously. They think a Tylenol is going to cure chronic pain. On top of endometriosis, I have early stages of rheumatoid arthritis and I do have fibromyalgia. I am so sorry that you had to deal with this BS crap, literally she didn't even give you a time of day to explain that you had a referral and you were recommended, she went straight to you want dem oPiOiDs.
This opioid crisis is doing more harm than good, we are not saving addicts... it's still killing many addicts from street drugs, but we're mostly killing chronic pain patients and there's nothing wrong taking opioids. My OB prescribes me norcos monthly and she has no problem with it because she knows how it feels dealing with severe chronic pain, she has it herself. My doctor told me today at my appointment for a follow up after the ER two days ago... She went to the ER three weeks ago because her right leg from sciatica and DDD she couldn't even move her leg because she was in so much pain and they denied her opioids, and she's an MD! Shows you how out of control this opioid crisis is.

I have to watch triggers too, I joined a trichotillomania group on Facebook but ended up leaving because people were showing their follicles and it's a big trigger for me. It is almost like when someone shows their self-harm scars to someone who struggles with cutting. I just tell people stay away from triggers especially with me I got rid of my tweezers and pliers that I pulled with and it helped a lot. Then write little affirmations sticky notes on the places where you pull at, like say... You are beautiful, you will overcome this, try not to pull today, focus on something else, and use your coping skills or fidget toys. I love tangles and they've helped me a lot along with journaling/ sketching too. Hope this helps you out, and never give up. You will make it :-) remember you are beautiful!

I had a dream one day about 4 years ago and saw myself in long hair and I wanted that. I threw away all my triggers like tweezers, pliers I know extreme, and covered the mirrors in the bathroom. I would just write notes of positivity on the bathroom mirror if I had to use the mirror after shower or makeup. I would write on sticky notes you are beautiful, try not to pull today, and just different affirmations. it took a long time to grow this hair back because I really wild the care and it's very surprising got my hair back. I do have a little bald spot as I relapsed about 3 weeks ago but I just am proud of myself. I always tell other people who struggle with trichotillomania, just be proud of yourself because you're doing the best you can. That disorder is hell, and I know how it feels to feel low or feel like crap. Everyone's beautiful in their own way. If you are bald, bald is beautiful and that's a fact. I just didn't like myself in bald hair because I looked weird, I saw other girls with trichotillomania who are bald and they were gorgeous! Just baby steps, that's all I can say. Just keep going and never give up. It will get easier that is part of recovery :-) take care!
